## ⭐ Self-correction by the filing seat — the root cause in the original body was WRONG

`domain:spec` seat, `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-14T14:0xZ. The body is rewritten; this comment records what changed and why, so the correction is an event and ⛔ not a silent edit.

**What I filed:** that this container has **no** Claude-App write channel, and that the rule 「内容恒经 REST 代理(`claude[bot]`)」 is therefore unsatisfiable here.

**What is true:** `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/comments/5664585381` returns **`performed_via_github_app.slug: "claude"`** (App id `1236702`, owner `anthropics`). ⇒ **The App IS the writer.** The byline differs because it uses a **user-to-server** token, which GitHub attributes to the acting user (`user.login: "os-warren"`, `type: "User"`) while stamping `performed_via_github_app`. A `claude[bot]` byline comes from a **server-to-server (installation)** token.

⇒ 「经 REST 代理」 is **satisfied**; only 「署名 `claude[bot]`」 is not. The finding survives; its mechanism does not.

**Why the error mattered enough to correct rather than let stand:** the original framing would have sent the skills seat to build a *missing channel* that already exists. The real question is much narrower — **which token type the existing App uses** — and it carries a cost the first version could not even see: a server-to-server token makes every seat write an indistinguishable `claude[bot]`, erasing the per-seat attribution this fleet's audit trail currently leans on (`os-bill`, `os-tesla`, `os-litant`, `os-justin`, `os-sales` all appear as distinct bylines in live threads). That trade-off is now in the body as the substance of the decision.

**How I found it:** I did not. The maintainer asked for `performed_via_github_app.slug` explicitly. ⛔ I had filed the card without ever reading that field — I inferred "no App channel" from `GET /user` returning a User account, which is exactly the 「判据取命令输出」 failure this repo keeps writing rules about: I had a reading (`user.login`), drew a mechanism from it, and never took the one reading that would have discriminated.

**Two further readings added to the body while correcting it:**
- `git config user.name/user.email` (local and `--global`) = **`Claude` / `noreply@anthropic.com`**, and dispatch-branch commits are authored `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` ⇒ **commits** and **comments** carry different bylines in the same container.
- The authoritative org-role endpoints are **unreadable from a seat container**: every `/orgs/...` path and even `/repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators/{user}/permission` is refused by the Claude proxy (`"Access to this GitHub API path is not permitted through this proxy."`, `documentation_url` → `docs.anthropic.com`), while `/repos/.../issues/6017` returns 200 as a live-credential control. ⇒ `author_association: COLLABORATOR` is the only org-ish signal available, and it is ⛔ suggestive, not authoritative.

The self-correction 5665274737 and the channel reading on #18158 (5665982929) are the record of what the mechanism turned out to be. `finding` dropped at close; nothing left to build.
